Friday, 11 pm
Today at the canteen I sat with Arnab's group for the first time. They're the band kids, the ones everyone knows. They were talking about who likes whom, and Arnab turned to me: "You're friends with Moumita, na? Does she like anyone?"
And I said it. That she likes Ritwik from Section C. Everyone went "ooh" and Arnab laughed: "This girl knows all the gossip!" I felt... included. Like I'd paid an entry fee.
On the walk home I told myself it was nothing. Everyone has crushes. It's not like I told them about her dad's job.
But now it's night and I keep seeing Moumita's face when she told me, how she made me pinky-swear. Ritwik goes to Arnab's tuition. Of course he'll hear.
I feel sick. I wanted them to find me interesting, and I used her to do it.
Kalyani

qa.q: What did Kalyani reveal about Moumita?
qa.a: Kalyani said that Moumita likes Ritwik from Section C.

qa.q: Why did Kalyani tell Moumita's secret at the canteen?
qa.a: Kalyani wanted Arnab's group to find her interesting, and when everyone reacted she felt included, like paying an entry fee.

qa.q: What turning point is open to Kalyani now?
qa.a: Kalyani could tell Moumita herself tomorrow, before Ritwik hears it from others, apologise without excuses and accept that Moumita may be angry.

qa.q: What might Moumita go through if the secret reaches Ritwik?
qa.a: Moumita could feel exposed and embarrassed, and deeply hurt that the pinky-swear meant so little.

grounding: Shows a teenage girl letting a friend's secret slip to seem interesting to a new group, calling it no big deal at first and feeling its weight later.

You want to know how it happened? Fine. I'm Alka, and I'm not proud of it.

The new girls in our tuition batch were the cool ones. They had inside jokes, they went to cafés after class. On Thursday they let me sit with them, and I was so desperate to have something to say.

One of them said, "Simran's so quiet. Is she boring or what?"

And I said, "She's not boring. She's got a massive crush on Kunal. Like, writes-his-name-in-her-notebook massive."

They screamed. I felt interesting for once. I told myself it didn't matter, it was a small thing, everyone has crushes.

Then on the auto home I remembered Simran's face when she told me, how she'd made me pinky-swear. My stomach turned over. I couldn't sleep that night.

qa.q: What did Simran make Alka do when she told her secret?
qa.a: Pinky-swear.

qa.q: Why did Alka tell Simran's secret to the new girls?
qa.a: She wanted to seem interesting and fit in with the cool girls, and felt desperate to have something to say.

qa.q: What could Alka do now that she feels the weight of it?
qa.a: She could tell Simran honestly what she did before Simran hears it from others, and apologise without excuses.

qa.q: How might Simran feel if she finds out?
qa.a: She would likely feel betrayed and humiliated, since she trusted Alka and made her pinky-swear.

grounding: Alka lets Simran's secret slip to seem interesting to a new group, tells herself it's no big deal, then later feels the weight of what she did.

Saturday. At Priyanka's birthday sleepover, the older girls were trading gossip in the dark, and Madhuri, new to the group, wanted badly to be one of them. When someone asked about Ayesha, Madhuri heard herself say, "Her parents are getting divorced. She told me." There was a gasp. Someone said, "No way." Madhuri felt important for about ten seconds.

Sunday. She told herself it was fine. Everyone's parents fought. It wasn't like she'd posted it anywhere.

Tuesday. Ayesha didn't come to school. Madhuri saw two of the girls from the sleepover whispering and glancing at Ayesha's empty desk. Her stomach dropped.

Wednesday. Ayesha came back, eyes puffy, and sat alone at lunch. Madhuri stood holding her tray, knowing exactly why, and feeling it all at once: the gasp, the ten seconds, and Ayesha trusting her with it in the first place.

qa.q: Where did Madhuri reveal Ayesha's secret?
qa.a: At Priyanka's birthday sleepover.

qa.q: How does Madhuri's feeling change from Saturday to Wednesday?
qa.a: At first she felt important, then told herself it was fine, but by Wednesday she feels guilty and ashamed, realising the harm she caused.

qa.q: What could Madhuri do at this stage?
qa.a: She could go to Ayesha, admit she told the secret, apologise without excuses, and ask the girls to stop spreading it.

qa.q: What is it like for Ayesha sitting alone at lunch?
qa.a: She is likely hurt and humiliated, maybe confused about how the secret got out, and feeling alone at a hard time at home.

grounding: Over several days Madhuri lets slip Ayesha's secret to impress a new group, tells herself it doesn't matter, then feels the full weight of what she did.

Siddharth, you're angry because your friend told your secret. I understand. Let me tell you something your Preeti bua has never told anyone in this family.

When I was a girl of fifteen, in Indore, my best friend Sushma confided that her elder brother had failed his exams twice and her father had beaten the table in rage. She begged me to keep it quiet.

Then a group of senior girls invited me to sit with them at lunch. They were so glamorous. They were talking about brothers, and I wanted to have a story too. So I told them Sushma's.

In the moment I thought, it's nothing, they'll forget. But the next morning, Sushma's face when she walked in, I can still see it. She knew immediately.

I should have gone to her that same day and told her myself. I didn't. I waited, and it cost me the friendship.

qa.q: What did the senior girls invite Preeti to do?
qa.a: To sit with them at lunch.

qa.q: Why did Preeti tell Sushma's secret?
qa.a: She wanted to seem interesting to the glamorous senior girls and have a story to share.

qa.q: What choice in the story does Preeti wish had been different?
qa.a: She wishes she had gone to Sushma that same day and admitted it herself instead of waiting.

qa.q: How did Sushma probably feel when she walked in the next morning?
qa.a: She was likely hurt and betrayed, knowing immediately that Preeti had told.

grounding: Preeti bua recalls letting her best friend's secret slip to impress senior girls, telling herself it was nothing, then feeling the weight of the betrayal.

Madhuri had exactly ten minutes before the bell, and the new group had finally let her sit with them on the steps.

Varun, who everyone wanted to impress, was telling a story about a teacher. Then someone said, "Madhuri, you're friends with Tanu, right? She's so quiet. Does she even like anyone?"

Everyone looked at her. For the first time, they were interested.

"Actually," Madhuri said, before she could stop herself, "she has a huge crush on Imtiaz. Like, huge."

The group burst into delighted noises. Varun grinned at her.

It's not a big deal, Madhuri told herself. Everyone has crushes. The bell rang, and she walked to class feeling like she belonged.

It was only that night, when she saw Tanu's message, "Why is everyone teasing me about Imtiaz??", that the weight of it hit her.

qa.q: How long did Madhuri have before the bell?
qa.a: She had exactly ten minutes before the bell.

qa.q: What was Madhuri feeling when she saw Tanu's message that night?
qa.a: She suddenly felt guilty and heavy, realising she'd betrayed Tanu's trust just to seem interesting.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Madhuri now?
qa.a: She could admit to Tanu that she told the group and apologise without excuses, and ask the group to stop teasing.

qa.q: How might Tanu feel when everyone starts teasing her?
qa.a: Tanu is likely confused, embarrassed and hurt, not yet knowing who revealed her secret.

grounding: Wanting to seem interesting to a new group, a teen lets slip a friend's secret, tells herself it is nothing and only later feels its weight.
